subject: maths
title: Multiplying and Dividing by 10 and 100: Place Value, Multiples of 10 and Missing Numbers
seo_title: Year 4 Multiplying and Dividing by 10 and 100 Worksheets: Free Maths with Answer Key (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Solve problems involving multiplying or dividing natural numbers by multiples and powers of 10 without a calculator, using the multiplicative relationship between the place value of digits
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on multiplying and dividing by 10 and 100, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4N05): moving digits on a place value chart, multiples of 10 and 100 like 30 × 4 and 600 ÷ 3, missing numbers and word problems with $10 notes and kilometres. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: × 10 moves every digit 1 place to the left; × 100 moves it 2 places. ÷ 10 and ÷ 100 move the digits right.
key_sub: 47 × 100 = 4700 and 3050 ÷ 10 = 305: zeros hold the empty places. For multiples of 10, use a fact: 3 × 4 = 12, so 30 × 4 = 12 tens = 120.
body_html:
Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right

When you multiply by 10, every digit becomes 10 times bigger, so it moves 1 place to the left. When you multiply by 100, every digit moves 2 places to the left. A 0 holds each empty place.

Dividing by 10 and 100

Dividing is the inverse. ÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right; ÷ 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right. Zeros drop off only from the end: one for ÷ 10, two for ÷ 100. Zeros in the middle stay.

Multiples of 10 and 100

Use a fact you know, then think about place value. 60 is 6 tens, so 60 × 7 is 6 × 7 = 42 tens = 420.

Multiply

300 × 4 = ?

300 is 3 hundreds. 3 × 4 = 12, so 300 × 4 = 12 hundreds.

Answer: 1200

Divide

2400 ÷ 6 = ?

2400 is 24 hundreds. 24 ÷ 6 = 4, so 2400 ÷ 6 = 4 hundreds. Check: 400 × 6 = 2400.

Answer: 400

Missing number

? × 100 = 3600

Work backwards with the inverse: 3600 ÷ 100 = 36.

Answer: 36

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing the 0 in the wrong place (36 × 10 = 306)Move every digit 1 place left; the 0 goes in the ones place: 360
Moving the wrong way (450 ÷ 10 = 4500)÷ makes a number smaller: digits move right, 450 ÷ 10 = 45
Taking off every zero (3050 ÷ 10 = 35)Only the end zero goes; the middle 0 still holds a place: 305
Dropping the zero from the fact (50 × 8 = 40)5 × 8 = 40, so 50 × 8 = 40 tens = 400
× 100 with only one zero (46 × 100 = 460)× 100 moves digits 2 places: 4600

faq.q: How do you multiply by 10 and 100 in Year 4?
faq.a: Every digit moves to a bigger place: 1 place to the left for × 10 and 2 places for × 100, with zeros holding the empty places. For example, 47 × 100 = 4700.

faq.q: Why is “just add a zero” not a good rule?
faq.a: It does not explain what happens and can put the zero in the wrong place, such as 36 × 10 = 306. It also breaks later with decimals: 0.4 × 10 is 4, not 0.40. Moving digits on a place value chart always works.

faq.q: What does AC9M4N05 mean in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: It is the Year 4 maths content description for multiplying and dividing natural numbers by multiples and powers of 10 without a calculator, using place value. For example, 30 × 4 = 120 and 600 ÷ 3 = 200.

faq.q: How can my child work out 30 × 4 in their head?
faq.a: Use the fact 3 × 4 = 12. 30 is 3 tens, so 30 × 4 is 12 tens, which is 120.

sets.title: × 10 and × 100 on a place value chart

items.q: Use the place value chart. What is 36 × 10?
items.e: × 10 moves every digit 1 place to the left: the 3 tens become 3 hundreds and the 6 ones become 6 tens. A 0 holds the ones place. 36 × 10 = 360.
× 10 moves every digit 1 place to the left: the 5 tens become 5 hundreds and the 8 ones become 8 tens. A 0 holds the ones place. 58 × 10 = 580.

items.q: When you multiply a number by 10, every digit moves …
items.e: × 10 makes every digit 10 times bigger, so each digit moves 1 place to the left. Example: 24 × 10 = 240.

items.q: Use the place value chart. What is 124 × 10?
items.e: × 10 moves every digit 1 place to the left: the 1 hundred becomes 1 thousand. A 0 holds the ones place. 124 × 10 = 1240.
× 100 moves every digit 2 places to the left: the 9 ones become 9 hundreds. Zeros hold the tens and ones places. 9 × 100 = 900. (9 × 10 = 90 moves the digits only 1 place.)

items.q: Use the place value chart. What is 46 × 100?
items.e: × 100 moves every digit 2 places to the left: the 4 tens become 4 thousands and the 6 ones become 6 hundreds. Zeros hold the tens and ones places. 46 × 100 = 4600. (46 × 10 = 460 moves the digits only 1 place.)

items.q: When you multiply a number by 100, every digit moves …
items.e: × 100 is × 10 and then × 10 again, so each digit moves 2 places to the left. Example: 24 × 100 = 2400.
× 10 moves every digit 1 place to the left: the 3 hundreds become 3 thousands and the 5 ones become 5 tens. A 0 holds the ones place. 305 × 10 = 3050.

× 100 moves every digit 2 places to the left: the 7 tens become 7 thousands and the 3 ones become 3 hundreds. Zeros hold the tens and ones places. 73 × 100 = 7300. (73 × 10 = 730 moves the digits only 1 place.)
× 10 moves every digit 1 place to the left: the 4 hundreds become 4 thousands and the 6 tens become 6 hundreds. A 0 holds the ones place. 460 × 10 = 4600.

items.q: Use the place value chart. What is 208 × 100?
items.e: × 100 moves every digit 2 places to the left: the 2 hundreds become 2 ten thousands and the 8 ones become 8 hundreds. Zeros hold the tens and ones places. 208 × 100 = 20 800. (208 × 10 = 2080 moves the digits only 1 place.)
× 10 moves every digit 1 place to the left: the 8 hundreds become 8 thousands and the 9 tens become 9 hundreds. A 0 holds the ones place. 890 × 10 = 8900.
× 10 moves every digit 1 place to the left: the 2 thousands become 2 ten thousands. A 0 holds the ones place. 2047 × 10 = 20 470.

× 100 moves every digit 2 places to the left: the 3 hundreds become 3 ten thousands and the 5 tens become 5 thousands. Zeros hold the tens and ones places. 350 × 100 = 35 000. (350 × 10 = 3500 moves the digits only 1 place.)
× 100 moves every digit 2 places to the left: the 1 hundred becomes 1 ten thousand. Zeros hold the tens and ones places. 125 × 100 = 12 500. (125 × 10 = 1250 moves the digits only 1 place.)
× 10 moves every digit 1 place to the left. The 4 tens move into the hundreds place: 47 × 10 = 470.
× 100 moves every digit 2 places to the left: ones → tens → hundreds. 63 × 100 = 6300.

items.q: 52 has changed to 5200. What was 52 multiplied by?
items.e: The 5 tens became 5 thousands: every digit moved 2 places to the left. That is × 100. Count the new zeros: 52 → 5200 has 2 more zeros.

items.q: 805 has changed to 8050. What was 805 multiplied by?
items.e: The 8 hundreds became 8 thousands: every digit moved 1 place to the left. That is × 10. The 0 inside 805 moves too, so the answer is 8050, not 8500.

items.q: Which number is 10 times as large as 380?
items.e: 10 times as large means × 10. Every digit moves 1 place to the left: 380 × 10 = 3800. (390 is only 10 more.)

sets.title: ÷ 10 and ÷ 100 of numbers ending in zeros

items.e: ÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right: the 6 hundreds become 6 tens. 600 ÷ 10 = 60. Only one zero from the end drops off; any other zeros still hold places.

items.q: Use the place value chart. What is 4500 ÷ 10?
items.e: ÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right: the 4 thousands become 4 hundreds and the 5 hundreds become 5 tens. 4500 ÷ 10 = 450. Only one zero from the end drops off; any other zeros still hold places.
÷ 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right: the 8 hundreds become 8 ones. 800 ÷ 100 = 8.

÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right: the 3 thousands become 3 hundreds and the 6 hundreds become 6 tens. 3600 ÷ 10 = 360. Only one zero from the end drops off; any other zeros still hold places.

items.q: When you divide a number by 100, every digit moves …
items.e: ÷ 100 makes every digit 100 times smaller, so each digit moves 2 places to the right. Example: 2400 ÷ 100 = 24.

items.q: Use the place value chart. What is 4700 ÷ 100?
items.e: ÷ 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right: the 4 thousands become 4 tens and the 7 hundreds become 7 ones. 4700 ÷ 100 = 47.
÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right: the 9 hundreds become 9 tens. 900 ÷ 10 = 90. Only one zero from the end drops off; any other zeros still hold places.
÷ 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right: the 6 thousands become 6 tens. 6000 ÷ 100 = 60. Only two zeros from the end drop off; any other zeros still hold places.

items.q: Use the place value chart. What is 2080 ÷ 10?
items.e: ÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right: the 2 thousands become 2 hundreds and the 8 tens become 8 ones. 2080 ÷ 10 = 208. Only one zero from the end drops off; any other zeros still hold places.
÷ 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right: thousands → hundreds → tens. 4300 ÷ 100 = 43.
÷ 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right: the 9 thousands become 9 tens and the 3 hundreds become 3 ones. 9300 ÷ 100 = 93.

÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right: the 4 ten thousands become 4 thousands and the 5 hundreds become 5 tens. 40 500 ÷ 10 = 4050. Only one zero from the end drops off; any other zeros still hold places.

items.q: Use the place value chart. What is 2400 ÷ 100?
items.e: ÷ 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right: the 2 thousands become 2 tens and the 4 hundreds become 4 ones. 2400 ÷ 100 = 24.
÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right: the 5 thousands become 5 hundreds and the 1 ten becomes 1 one. 5010 ÷ 10 = 501. Only one zero from the end drops off; any other zeros still hold places.

÷ 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right: the 1 ten thousand becomes 1 hundred and the 2 thousands become 2 tens. 12 000 ÷ 100 = 120. Only two zeros from the end drop off; any other zeros still hold places.
÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right: the 1 ten thousand becomes 1 thousand. 12 300 ÷ 10 = 1230. Only one zero from the end drops off; any other zeros still hold places.

÷ 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right: the 3 ten thousands become 3 hundreds and the 5 hundreds become 5 ones. 30 500 ÷ 100 = 305. Only two zeros from the end drop off; any other zeros still hold places.
÷ 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right: the 5 ten thousands become 5 hundreds. 50 000 ÷ 100 = 500. Only two zeros from the end drop off; any other zeros still hold places.
÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right, so 800 ÷ 10 = 80. 800 ÷ 100 = 8, and 80 ÷ 10 = 8.

items.q: Mei says 3050 ÷ 10 = 35 because “you take off the zeros”. What is 3050 ÷ 10?
items.e: ÷ 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right: the 3 thousands become 3 hundreds and the 5 tens become 5 ones. The 0 in the hundreds place moves to the tens place and must stay. 3050 ÷ 10 = 305.
60 is 6 tens. 6 × 5 = 30, so 60 × 5 = 30 tens = 300. The 0 in 30 is part of the fact, so keep it as well.
200 is 2 hundreds. 2 × 7 = 14, so 200 × 7 = 14 hundreds = 1400.
300 is 3 hundreds. 3 × 6 = 18, so 300 × 6 = 18 hundreds = 1800.
600 is 6 hundreds. 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so 600 ÷ 3 = 2 hundreds = 200. Check: 200 × 3 = 600.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 70 × 6?

items.e: 50 is 5 tens. 5 × 8 = 40, so 50 × 8 = 40 tens = 400. The 0 in 40 is part of the fact, so keep it as well.
500 is 5 hundreds. 5 × 6 = 30, so 500 × 6 = 30 hundreds = 3000. The 0 in 30 is part of the fact, so keep it as well.
800 is 8 hundreds. 8 × 4 = 32, so 800 × 4 = 32 hundreds = 3200.
700 is 7 hundreds. 7 × 8 = 56, so 700 × 8 = 56 hundreds = 5600.
Use 4 × 2 = 8. 4 tens × 2 tens = 8 hundreds, so put back two zeros: 40 × 20 = 800.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 3600 ÷ 9?
items.e: 3600 is 36 hundreds. Use 36 ÷ 9 = 4: 36 hundreds ÷ 9 = 4 hundreds, so 3600 ÷ 9 = 400.
Work backwards: 380 ÷ 10 = 38. Check: 38 × 10 = 380.
Work backwards: 4500 ÷ 100 moves the digits 2 places to the right, so the missing number is 45. 450 × 100 would be 45 000.
The 7 tens became 7 thousands, so the digits moved 2 places to the left. That is × 100.
The digits moved 1 place to the left, so 64 × 10 = 640. (576 is 640 − 64: that is subtracting, not multiplying.)
Work backwards with the inverse: 60 × 10 = 600. Check: 600 ÷ 10 = 60.
Work backwards with the inverse: 23 × 100 = 2300. Check: 2300 ÷ 100 = 23.
The 8 thousands became 8 tens: the digits moved 2 places to the right. That is ÷ 100.
The digits moved 1 place to the right: 950 ÷ 10 = 95. (855 is 950 − 95: that is subtracting.)
450 = 45 × 10, so there are 45 tens in 450. The 5 is only the tens digit; the 4 hundreds are 40 more tens.
3200 = 32 × 100, so there are 32 hundreds. The 2 is only the hundreds digit; the 3 thousands are 30 more hundreds.
Use 6 × 4 = 24. 240 is 24 tens, so the missing number is 6 tens = 60. Check: 60 × 4 = 240.
Use 7 × 5 = 35. 350 is 35 tens, so the missing number is 5 tens = 50. Check: 7 × 50 = 350.
Use 6 × 3 = 18. 1800 is 18 hundreds, so the missing number is 6 hundreds = 600. Check: 600 × 3 = 1800.
400 is 4 hundreds and 2800 is 28 hundreds. 4 × 7 = 28, so the missing number is 7. Check: 400 × 7 = 2800.
Think 9 tens × ? = 36 tens. 9 × 4 = 36, so the missing number is 4. Check: 360 ÷ 4 = 90. (270 is 360 − 90: that is subtracting.)
Use the inverse: 30 × 5 = 3 tens × 5 = 15 tens = 150. Check: 150 ÷ 5 = 30. (6 is 30 ÷ 5, the wrong operation.)

sets.title: Word problems: boxes of 100, $10 notes and 1000 m in a km

items.q: Pencils come in boxes of 100. The school office orders 24 boxes. How many pencils is that?
items.e: 24 boxes × 100 pencils. × 100 moves the digits 2 places to the left: 24 × 100 = 2400 pencils.

items.q: Each of the 28 students in Year 4 brings a $10 note for the school excursion. How much money is that?
items.e: 28 students × $10. × 10 moves the digits 1 place to the left: 28 × 10 = $280.

items.q: Isla has saved $450, all in $10 notes. How many $10 notes does she have?
items.e: How many tens are in 450? 450 ÷ 10 = 45 notes. Check: 45 × $10 = $450.

items.q: The P&C raised $3600 at the school fete. The treasurer counts it all in $100 notes. How many notes is that?
items.e: 3600 ÷ 100 moves the digits 2 places to the right: 36 notes. Check: 36 × $100 = $3600.

items.q: 1 km = 1000 m. The school cross-country course is 2 km long. How many metres is that?
items.e: Each kilometre is 1000 m, so 2 km = 2 × 1000 m = 2000 m.

items.q: A fun run in Perth is 5000 m long. How many kilometres is that?
items.e: 1000 m = 1 km. 5000 m is 5 thousands of metres, so it is 5 km. (5000 km would take days to drive!)
Each dollar is 100c, so $8 = 8 × 100c = 800c.

items.q: Jack empties his money box. It has 40 coins, and every coin is 10c. How much money is that?
1 cm = 10 mm. A new pencil is 18 cm long. How long is it in millimetres?
items.e: Each centimetre is 10 mm, so 18 cm = 18 × 10 mm = 180 mm.

items.q: 1 m = 100 cm. The classroom is 9 m long. How long is it in centimetres?
items.e: Each metre is 100 cm, so 9 m = 9 × 100 cm = 900 cm.

items.q: At the school sausage sizzle, each class gets 30 sausages. There are 8 classes. How many sausages are needed?
items.e: 8 × 3 = 24, so 30 × 8 = 24 tens = 240 sausages.

items.q: A footy club has 600 raffle tickets. Three teams share them equally to sell. How many tickets does each team get?
items.e: 600 is 6 hundreds. 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so 600 ÷ 3 = 2 hundreds = 200 tickets. Check: 200 × 3 = 600.

items.q: A bakery puts 480 bread rolls into bags of 10. How many bags does it fill?
items.e: 480 ÷ 10 moves the digits 1 place to the right: 48 bags. Check: 48 × 10 = 480.

items.q: Tea bags come in boxes of 100. The school canteen uses 1500 tea bags in a term. How many boxes is that?
items.e: 1500 ÷ 100 moves the digits 2 places to the right: 15 boxes. Check: 15 × 100 = 1500.

items.q: A wildlife park orders 6 bags of kangaroo food. Each bag holds 20 kg. How many kilograms is that?
One lap of the school oval is 400 m. William runs 5 laps at the athletics carnival. How far does he run?
items.e: 4 × 5 = 20, so 400 × 5 = 20 hundreds = 2000 m. That is 2 km. The 0 in 20 is part of the fact, so keep it.

items.q: A water truck carries 900 L to a farm each day. How much water does it carry in 3 days?
The school orders 4 boxes of 100 pencils and 6 packs of 10 pencils. How many pencils is that altogether?
items.e: Boxes: 4 × 100 = 400. Packs: 6 × 10 = 60. Total: 400 + 60 = 460 pencils. (1000 treats the packs as 100s; 406 forgets that each pack has 10.)

items.q: Cooper puts $10 into his savings every week for 20 weeks. Then he spends $150 on a new bike helmet and lights. How much does he have left?
items.e: Step 1: 20 × $10 = $200. Step 2: $200 − $150 = $50. ($200 is only step 1; $350 adds instead of subtracting; $1850 comes from 20 × $10 = $2000, one zero too many.)

items.q: Aarav rides 3 km to netball training. Ethan rides 2800 m to footy training. How much further does Aarav ride?
items.e: Change km to m first: 3 km = 3 × 1000 m = 3000 m. Then 3000 − 2800 = 200 m. (2797 comes from 2800 − 3 without changing the units.)
